summary: Find multiplayer games more easily, browse a cleaner Games library, and explore your update history—even offline.
introduction: Version 1.4.0 introduces multiplayer filtering, an in-app release history, and several interface refinements that make Earnings Tracker easier to navigate and use.
upgradeNotes: Before upgrading, keep an independent backup of your application data.
On first launch, Earnings Tracker adds new multiplayer metadata fields to the existing game catalog. This migration preserves your financial records, ownership information, and history.

sections.heading: 🎮 Multiplayer Game Filtering
changes: Multiplayer filter — Quickly find games with reviewed multiplayer support in the Games library.
Verified information — Games with unknown multiplayer support are excluded from the filter, helping keep results relevant.
Updated catalog — The bundled game catalog now includes reviewed multiplayer information and supporting evidence.

sections.heading: 📋 In-App Release History
changes: Browse past releases and their changes without leaving the application.
View release dates and identify your currently installed version.
Access the release history even without an internet connection.

sections.heading: Cleaner Games Library
changes: Reorganized filters — Frequently used options are easier to access, while additional filters are grouped under More filters.
Smarter filter controls — Clear active filters without losing your preferred sort order or archived-game visibility.
Searchable dropdowns — Find options more easily without scrolling through long lists.
Refined game rows — Improved presentation makes game information easier to scan.

sections.heading: Interface and Usability
changes: Improved scrolling behavior for a smoother browsing experience.
Refined session controls for a cleaner interface.
Updated chart presentation for better visual consistency.

summary: Choose which payment covers a session and see which games you own on Steam.
upgradeNotes: Keep a separate backup before upgrading. When you first open this version, the app updates your saved data so sessions can be linked to payments. Older sessions continue to count toward payments by date unless you change their payment assignment.

sections.heading: Added
changes: Link verified sessions to Current payout or to a payment marked Paid or Processing. See which sessions a payment covers and compare their earnings with the payment amount.

Change which payment an older session belongs to in the session editor. The app keeps a record of each change. Older sessions that you verify now go into Current payout unless they already have a payment assigned.
Connect your Steam profile using a personal Steam Web API key to show and filter games you own. Refresh your Steam library yourself, or let the app check when you open Games, at most once a day.

sections.heading: Improved
changes: Easier-to-read money summaries, payment details, import results, Settings messages, and bookmark buttons.
Cleaner Games and Game Details pages, with shorter Game Pass descriptions. You can still see when availability was checked, when access expires, and when information may be out of date.

sections.heading: Using Steam
changes: Set Game details to Public in Steam so the app can reliably check your library. If a check fails, your last saved library stays available. Games you mark as owned yourself and purchase costs you enter are kept separately.
Your Steam API key is stored securely by Windows and is not included in backups. Backups do include your linked Steam account ID and last saved library.

summary: A fresh look for Dashboard, Sessions, and Games, with easier browsing.

sections.heading: Improved
changes: Dashboard shows how your earnings change over time, session statuses, time played, top earning games, and money summaries.
Find sessions with search, sorting, and filters for game, status, or date. View or edit session details and open the related game from a compact list that handles large histories.
Browse more games at once, with clearer earning rates and availability. Filter and sort games, check ownership, use bookmarks, show archived games, and keep your browsing preferences.
More consistent navigation and session review, save, and cancel controls. The app still checks entries and keeps a history of changes.

sections.heading: About this update
changes: This update changes how the app looks and feels. Your saved financial records and earnings calculations stay the same. Steam features were not yet available in this version.

summary: Keep your data separate from the app, make backups, and import sessions more reliably.
upgradeNotes: If you use version 1.0.0, install this version separately. The update button in version 1.0.0 cannot install it because Windows treats it as a different app.

Before upgrading from 1.0.0, close the old app and keep a separate backup. Install the new version alongside it. On first launch, the new app copies and checks the records and backups it can transfer, keeping the originals. Check your history and backups in the new app before relying on it. Keep the old app closed, and do not uninstall or repair it until you have confirmed your data is safe.

sections.heading: Added
changes: Your records are stored separately from the app's files, so repairing or reinstalling the app does not require replacing your saved data.
Create and restore backups in Settings. Before restoring, the app checks the backup, asks you to confirm, and saves a recovery copy of your current data. A restart finishes the restore.
Games remembers your sort order, whether to show only bookmarked games, and whether to show archived games.

sections.heading: Fixed
changes: More reliable imports and session editing when several actions happen at once. Better checks help prevent duplicates and stop you from saving an import preview or edit based on outdated records.
Better handling when saved data is busy, two changes conflict, or the app cannot open or update its data files.

sections.heading: Updates
changes: App updates download the full application. Importing sessions through Add Session on Game Details was not yet available in this version.

summary: The first stable Windows release for tracking Nerve sessions and earnings.

sections.heading: Added
changes: Dashboard with verified earnings, recent sessions, and daily totals.
See each game's earning rate, earning limit, and your progress toward that limit.
Import sessions from Nerve's Recordings page, see their verification status, and review game matches when more than one game could fit.
Payment history for payments, bonuses, corrections, and adjustments that add to or subtract from your earnings.
Statistics to review your earnings over time and compare performance.
Check for and download app updates in Settings, then restart when you are ready. The game catalog can be updated separately.

sections.heading: About this version
changes: Your records are saved on your computer. This version runs on 64-bit Windows and includes what it needs to run. Sessions can be imported from Nerve's Recordings page; importing from Game Details was not yet available.
